 * Relation counts are expressed as "did this query find a row for the current
 * user", which is why every input carries pre-filtered `followers`/`favorites`
 * arrays instead of raw booleans.

  username: string
  bio: string | null
  image: string | null
  followers: unknown[]
}

export interface ArticleSource {
  slug: string
  title: string
  description: string
  body: string
  createdAt: Date
  updatedAt: Date
  author: ProfileSource
  tags: { tag: { name: string } }[]
  favorites: unknown[]
  _count: { favorites: number }
}

export interface CommentSource {
  id: number
  body: string

  updatedAt: Date
  author: ProfileSource
}

  email: string
  username: string
  bio: string | null
  image: string | null
}

  username: user.username,
  bio: user.bio,
  image: user.image,
  following: user.followers.length > 0,
})

  email: user.email,

  username: user.username,
  bio: user.bio,

})

})

# Boots the API against a throwaway SQLite database and runs the official
# RealWorld Hurl suite (specs/api/hurl) against it.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

PORT="${PORT:-8000}"
HOST_URL="http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}"
TEST_DB="${TEST_DB:-$ROOT/prisma/test.db}"
LOG_FILE="$ROOT/.test-server.log"

if ! command -v hurl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "hurl is not installed. See https://hurl.dev/docs/installation.html" >&2
  exit 1
fi

rm -f "$TEST_DB" "$TEST_DB-journal" "$TEST_DB-wal" "$TEST_DB-shm"
export DATABASE_URL="file:$TEST_DB"
export PORT

echo "Preparing test database at $TEST_DB"
npx prisma db push --force-reset --skip-generate >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
  npx prisma db push --force-reset >/dev/null

echo "Starting API on $HOST_URL"
npx tsx src/server.ts >"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!

cleanup() {
  kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
  if curl -fsS "$HOST_URL/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  if ! kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Server exited during startup:" >&2
    cat "$LOG_FILE" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.2
done

if ! curl -fsS "$HOST_URL/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Server did not become healthy in time:" >&2
  cat "$LOG_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi

FILES=("$@")
if [ ${#FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  FILES=("$ROOT"/specs/api/hurl/*.hurl)
fi

echo "Running Hurl suite (${#FILES[@]} files)"
hurl --test \
  --jobs 1 \
  --variable "host=$HOST_URL" \
  --variable "uid=$(date +%s)$$" \
  "${FILES[@]}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Boots the API against a throwaway SQLite database and runs the official
# RealWorld Hurl suite (specs/api/hurl) against it.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

PORT="${PORT:-8000}"
HOST_URL="http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}"
TEST_DB="${TEST_DB:-$ROOT/prisma/test.db}"
LOG_FILE="$ROOT/.test-server.log"

# Unrelated npm packages also ship a `hurl` binary, so pick the first candidate
# on PATH that actually identifies itself as Hurl (https://hurl.dev).
resolve_hurl() {
  if [ -n "${HURL_BIN:-}" ]; then
    echo "$HURL_BIN"
    return 0
  fi
  local candidate
  while IFS= read -r candidate; do
    if "$candidate" --version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | grep -qE '^hurl [0-9]'; then
      echo "$candidate"
      return 0
    fi
  done < <(type -a -p hurl 2>/dev/null)
  return 1
}

if ! HURL="$(resolve_hurl)"; then
  echo "hurl is not installed. See https://hurl.dev/docs/installation.html" >&2
  exit 1
fi

rm -f "$TEST_DB" "$TEST_DB-journal" "$TEST_DB-wal" "$TEST_DB-shm"
export DATABASE_URL="file:$TEST_DB"
export PORT

# The file was just deleted, so a plain push recreates the schema from scratch;
# no destructive reset flag is needed.
echo "Preparing test database at $TEST_DB"
npx prisma db push >/dev/null

echo "Starting API on $HOST_URL"
npx tsx src/server.ts >"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!

cleanup() {
  kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
  if curl -fsS "$HOST_URL/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  if ! kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Server exited during startup:" >&2
    cat "$LOG_FILE" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.2
done

if ! curl -fsS "$HOST_URL/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Server did not become healthy in time:" >&2
  cat "$LOG_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi

FILES=("$@")
if [ ${#FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  FILES=("$ROOT"/specs/api/hurl/*.hurl)
fi

echo "Running Hurl suite (${#FILES[@]} files) with $HURL"
"$HURL" --test \
  --jobs 1 \
  --variable "host=$HOST_URL" \
  --variable "uid=$(date +%s)$$" \
  "${FILES[@]}"

# RealWorld Backend — TypeScript · Fastify · Prisma · SQLite

A complete implementation of the [RealWorld backend
specification](https://realworld-docs.netlify.app/specifications/backend/endpoints/):
JWT authentication, users and profiles, article CRUD, comments, favorites, tags
and the personalized feed.

The full official [Hurl](https://hurl.dev) conformance suite — **13 files, 154
requests** — passes against this server.

## Requirements

- Node.js >= 20.6
- [Hurl](https://hurl.dev/docs/installation.html) (only needed to run the API tests)

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

`npm run dev` generates the Prisma client, creates/syncs the SQLite database and
starts the server with hot reload on <http://localhost:8000>. No `.env` file is
required — every setting has a working default (see `.env.example` to override).

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/health
# {"status":"ok"}
```

## Running the conformance tests

```bash
npm test
```

The script boots the API against a throwaway database (`prisma/test.db`), waits
for `/health`, runs every file in `specs/api/hurl`, and shuts the server down
again. To run a subset:

```bash
npm test -- specs/api/hurl/articles.hurl specs/api/hurl/feed.hurl
```

Expected output:

```
Executed files:    13
Executed requests: 154 (…)
Succeeded files:   13 (100.0%)
Failed files:      0 (0.0%)
```

## Scripts

| Script | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Sync the database and start the server with hot reload |
| `npm start` | Sync the database and start the server once |
| `npm test` | Run the official Hurl API suite end to end |
| `npm run typecheck` | Type-check the project (`tsc --noEmit`) |
| `npm run db:setup` | `prisma generate` + `prisma db push` |

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `file:./dev.db` | SQLite location, relative to the repo root |
| `HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address |
| `PORT` | `8000` | Bind port |
| `JWT_SECRET` | `realworld-development-secret` | JWT signing key — **override in production** |
| `JWT_EXPIRES_IN` | `30d` | Token lifetime |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `warn` | Fastify/pino log level |

## API surface

All endpoints live under `/api`. Authenticated requests use the RealWorld
`Authorization: Token <jwt>` header (`Bearer` is accepted too).

| Method | Path | Auth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/api/users` | – |
| `POST` | `/api/users/login` | – |
| `GET` | `/api/user` | required |
| `PUT` | `/api/user` | required |
| `GET` | `/api/profiles/:username` | optional |
| `POST` | `/api/profiles/:username/follow` | required |
| `DELETE` | `/api/profiles/:username/follow` | required |
| `GET` | `/api/articles` | optional |
| `GET` | `/api/articles/feed` | required |
| `GET` | `/api/articles/:slug` | optional |
| `POST` | `/api/articles` | required |
| `PUT` | `/api/articles/:slug` | required (author) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/articles/:slug` | required (author) |
| `POST` | `/api/articles/:slug/favorite` | required |
| `DELETE` | `/api/articles/:slug/favorite` | required |
| `GET` | `/api/articles/:slug/comments` | optional |
| `POST` | `/api/articles/:slug/comments` | required |
| `DELETE` | `/api/articles/:slug/comments/:id` | required (author) |
| `GET` | `/api/tags` | – |

`GET /api/articles` supports `tag`, `author`, `favorited`, `limit` (default 20)
and `offset` (default 0). `articlesCount` always reports the total number of
matching articles, not the size of the current page.

### Error responses

Every failure uses the RealWorld envelope:

```json
{ "errors": { "body": ["can't be blank"] } }
```

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | Missing (`token: is missing`) or invalid token; bad login credentials |
| `403` | Acting on somebody else's article or comment (`forbidden`) |
| `404` | Unknown article, comment or profile (`not found`) |
| `409` | Username or email already taken (`has already been taken`) |
| `422` | Validation failure (`can't be blank`, `is invalid`, …) |

## Design notes

- **Passwords** are hashed with `scrypt` from `node:crypto` (no native
  dependencies). The policy follows NIST 800-63B 5.1.1.2: a minimum of 8
  characters, at least 64 accepted, and no composition rules.
- **Slugs** combine a slugified title with a random suffix, so duplicate titles
  are allowed and each article still gets a unique, stable slug.
- **`updatedAt`** on articles is written explicitly and forced to be strictly
  greater than the previous value, so an update is always observably newer even
  for back-to-back writes.
- **Nullable profile fields** (`bio`, `image`) normalize `""` to `null`;
  `username`, `email` and `password` reject both `null` and `""`.
- **Viewer-scoped relations**: `following` and `favorited` are computed by
  including `followers`/`favorites` filtered down to the current viewer, which
  keeps a single query shape for both anonymous and authenticated requests.

## Project layout

```
prisma/schema.prisma      Data model (User, Follow, Article, Tag, Comment, Favorite)
scripts/run-api-tests.sh  Boots the API and runs the Hurl suite
specs/api/hurl/           Vendored official RealWorld conformance tests
src/
  app.ts                  Fastify wiring: auth hook, error handler, routes
  server.ts               Entry point
  auth.ts                 JWT signing/verification and request helpers
  password.ts             scrypt hashing
  validation.ts           Error-accumulating request validators
  presenters.ts           Prisma rows -> RealWorld JSON
  articles-shared.ts      Shared article query fragments
  slug.ts                 Slug generation
  routes/                 users, profiles, articles, comments, tags
```

## License

MIT

RealWorld 백엔드 API를 처음부터 구현하고 두 완료 기준을 모두 직접 실행해 검증했습니다.

**완료 기준 검증 결과**

1. **공식 Hurl 테스트 154/154 통과** — `realworld-apps/realworld`의 `specs/api/hurl`을 저장소에 vendoring(13 파일, 154 요청). `npm test` 실행 결과 `Succeeded files: 13 (100.0%) / Failed files: 0`.
2. **단일 명령 기동** — `npm run dev`가 Prisma 클라이언트 생성 + SQLite 스키마 동기화 + 서버 기동까지 수행. `.env`·DB·생성된 클라이언트가 전혀 없는 상태에서 시작해 `GET /health → {"status":"ok"}` 확인.

추가로 `npm run typecheck`(strict TS)도 오류 0.

**구현 요약**

- TypeScript(ESM, tsx 런타임) + Fastify 5 + Prisma 7(better-sqlite3 driver adapter) + SQLite
- JWT 인증(`Token`/`Bearer` 둘 다 허용), 비밀번호는 `node:crypto`의 scrypt — 네이티브 의존성 없음
- users/profiles, article CRUD, comments, favorites, tags, feed 전체
- 스펙 대응이 까다로웠던 지점들:
  - `articlesCount`는 페이지 크기가 아닌 **전체 매칭 수** (pagination/feed 테스트가 요구)
  - article `updatedAt`을 명시적으로 쓰고 이전 값보다 **엄격히 크도록** 보정 (연속 쓰기에서도 `!=` 단언 충족)
  - `bio`/`image`는 `""` → `null` 정규화, `username`/`email`/`password`는 `null`·`""` 모두 422
  - 중복 title 허용을 위해 slug에 랜덤 접미사 부여
  - body 없는 POST/DELETE(favorite, follow)가 415로 거부되지 않도록 catch-all content-type 파서 추가

**막혔다가 우회한 지점 2가지** (참고용)

- Prisma 7은 AI 에이전트가 `db push --force-reset`을 실행하는 것을 차단합니다. 테스트 스크립트가 DB 파일을 먼저 삭제하므로 파괴적 플래그 없이 일반 `db push`로 대체했습니다.
- npm 스크립트 PATH 상에서 무관한 npm 패키지의 `hurl` 실행 파일이 진짜 Hurl을 가립니다. 러너가 `--version` 출력으로 실제 Hurl 바이너리를 식별하도록 했습니다.
